Just a few thoughts here as a follow up.

The panel on the right hand side looks like it's based on a Google Maps local listing, because it hasn't been claimed and verified as a Google Business Profile. Unfortunately, anyone can submit edits to the Maps listings, and people often enter spurious phone numbers as a prank.

In this case, the Google Search results show that the business has a Facebook page, which gives a different phone number, so it would be worth suggesting an edit using what would appear to be their correct phone number from the Facebook page. I've already done that, but it wouldn't hurt for others to do the same.

The best solution would be to contact the owner of the business and suggest that they claim and verify the listing as a [Google Business Profile](https://www.google.com/business/). That way they will have control over the information shown.

Update: My edit appears to have been accepted, as I'm already seeing it updated in the panel.

If Google continues to reject your phone number update, there are two things you can try.

First, make a small change in another section of your Google Business Profile before trying again to update the phone number. For example, you can make some changes to your business description, upload a new photo, or adjust your business hours. Sometimes doing a little editing first helps bypass Google's automatic filters. After doing this, wait a day or two and then try updating your phone number again.

If the update still doesn't happen, provide stronger evidence by submitting documentation showing the correct phone number, such as your business license, lease, or utility bill. Also include online evidence, such as a screenshot of your website's contact page or links to trusted directories like Yelp or Facebook.

Additionally, update your number on third-party websites first, then wait a couple of days before trying the update again on Google. Mention this to Google, as it can help verify your number.

Does your business profile verified?

Guidelines for representing your business on Google

If your business either has a physical location that customers can visit, or travels to customers where they are, you can create a Business Profile on Google. To create a successful Business Profile that won’t be suspended requires that you:

- Avoid prohibited content. [Learn what content is prohibited](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177#illegal).
- Reflect your business accurately.
- Comply with the policies in this article.

Understand basic guidelines

To maintain high quality information on Google, follow this list of guidelines for local businesses. These guidelines can help you avoid common problems, including changes to your information or, in some cases, removal of your business information from Google.

For the best results managing your Business Profile:

- Represent your business as it’s consistently represented and recognized in the real world across signage, stationery, and other branding.
- Make sure your address and/or service area is accurate and precise.
- Choose the fewest number of categories it takes to describe your overall core business.
- There should only be one profile per business, as this can cause problems with how your information displays on Google Maps and Search.

Brands, organizations, artists, and other online-only businesses aren't eligible for Business Profiles.

Tip: If you’d like to get one-on-one guidance and tailored recommendations on how to make the most out of your profile, [book an appointment with Small Business Advisors](https://support.google.com/advisors).

Business eligibility & ownership

Eligible businesses

Ineligible businesses

The following businesses are not eligible for a Business Profile:

- Rental or for-sale properties such as vacation homes, model homes, or vacant apartments. Sales or leasing offices, however, are eligible for verification.
- An ongoing service, class, or meeting at a location that you don't own or have the authority to represent.
- Lead generation agents or companies.

Ownership

Additional guidelines for authorized representatives

Learn content guidelines for Business Profiles

Published content should highlight what makes your business unique.

Important: We do not allow content that contains private or confidential information such as personal financial information, government-issued IDs, contact information linked or associated with a name, sensitive records, images, transcripts or links that contain personal information. We also do not allow solicitation of the above information through local posts or a business description other than the user's own name, email, and phone number.

Business description

Name

Address

Use a precise, accurate address and/or service area to describe your business location. P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations aren't acceptable.

- Create your Business Profile for your actual, real-world location.
  - Suite numbers, floors, building numbers, and so on may also be included. Only include information like cross-streets and nearby landmarks in regions where the official street address doesn’t accurately pinpoint the business's location.
  - If you must specify a mailbox or suite number:
    - Enter your physical address as "Address Line 1."
    - Enter your mailbox or suite number as "Address Line 2."
  - If your business rents a physical mailing address but doesn't operate out of that location, also known as a virtual office, that location isn't eligible for a Business Profile.
  - Businesses can't list an office at a co-working space unless that office maintains clear signage, receives customers at the location during business hours, and is staffed during business hours by your business staff.
- Do not include information in address lines that doesn't pertain to your business’s physical location, like URLs or keywords.
- Do not create more than one page for each location of your business, either in a single account or multiple accounts.
  - Individual practitioners and departments within businesses, universities, hospitals, and government buildings may have separate pages. For more info, go to specific guidelines about [individual practitioners](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177#pract) and [departments](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177#departments).
- Businesses showing their address on Google should maintain permanent fixed signage of their business name at the address.
- If your address doesn't have a street number, or the system can't find it, you can [pin your business's location directly on the map](https://support.google.com/business/answer/6279343).

**Edit your Business Profile:**

You can edit your verified Business Profile on Google to keep your business information accurate and up to date. Update details like your address, hours, contact info, and photos to help customers find and learn more about your business.

[Manage your business](http://business.google.com/?skipLandingPage=true&gmbsrc=ww-ww-et-gs-z-gmb-v-z-h~bhc-core-u|mybb)

**Important** **:**

- If you haven’t already, [add or claim your business](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2911778), then [verify your Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242) so it's eligible to show up on Search, Maps, and other Google services.
- Your business must be verified before edits to the name, category, address, hours, phone number, website, and other details are published and appear on Google Search and Maps.
- Some business owners may still need to verify their business first before they edit their information.

**Edit a Business Profile**

You can edit your Business Profile directly on Google Search or Maps. Certain features to manage your profile may differ between Search and Maps and your device's operating system.

**Important:** To edit your business information:

- You must be signed in to the Google Account associated with your Business Profile.
- Your Business Profile must be verified.

Edit your Business Profile with Google Search

1. [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2. Click **Edit profile**.
3. After each change you make, click **Save**.

Edit your Business Profile with the Google Maps app

1. On your mobile device, open the Google Maps app.
2. At the bottom right, tap **Business**.
3. Tap **Edit profile**.
4. After each change you make, tap **Save.**

Types of edits

The following are some helpful tips for the types of information you can add or edit on your Business Profile.

[Check your edit status](https://support.google.com/business/workflow/15989794)

Business name

Category

Address and pin location

Service area

Hours

Phone

Chat

Website

Social media links

Attributes

Photos

If your Google Business profile is not available in public, there are a few things you can do to troubleshoot the issue:

1. Check your business information: Make sure that your business information is accurate and up-to-date. This includes your business name, address, phone number, website, and hours of operation. If any of this information is incorrect or outdated, it can affect the visibility of your profile in public.

2. Verify your business: If you haven't already done so, verify your business with Google. This involves confirming that you're the owner or manager of the business and providing additional information to prove your business's legitimacy. Once your business is verified, it will be more likely to show up in public search results.

3. Optimize your profile: Make sure that your Google Business profile is optimized for search engines. This includes adding high-quality photos, writing a compelling business description, and collecting customer reviews. The more complete and engaging your profile is, the more likely it is to show up in public search results.

4. Check your privacy settings: Make sure that your profile is set to "public" and that there are no privacy settings blocking its visibility. You can check this in your Google My Business dashboard under the "Settings" tab.

5. Contact Google support: If you've tried all of the above steps and your Google Business profile is still not available in public, you may need to contact Google support for further assistance. They can help you troubleshoot the issue and identify any technical problems that may be preventing your profile from showing up in public search results.
